DASH-28. Nothing distinguished 'quietly working' from 'died and nobody noticed': every existing signal (telemetry, the 5s Agent DOM poll, process facts) was evidence of activity, never an expectation of it. Design decision: trigger.schedule is free text ('weekdays at 08:00 local time') with no parseable structure, so deriving an expectation from it would mean parsing prose unreliably - added one small additive field instead, trigger.expected_interval_seconds, optional and meaningful only alongside type:schedule; absent means no derivable expectation and the agent is never marked stalled. stalled is deliberately NOT part of AgentStatus (the wire vocabulary an agent/runner may assert) but a new WorkspaceStatus = AgentStatus | 'stalled', computed only in lib/workspace.ts's buildOverview from timestamps the state snapshot already carries (runs/tasks/audit_events) - no new storage, no new polling, no runner changes. ONE of the three cases is proven end to end and two are unit tests only; the split matters more than the total, and ADR 0005 records the judgment behind it. PROVEN END TO END on the installed shell (proof 8, using the issue's numbering): case 2, the request the runner destroyed because its bounded buffer was full. A real agent the runner spawned fired 200 brokered requests past a buffer of 64 and the shell's own broker loop drained, recorded and rendered them - 200 sent, 64 adjudicated, 136 dropped, identical in all three runs, so it is a bound being hit rather than a race. 8d is the load-bearing check: audit rows plus dropped requests may not exceed what the agent actually sent, which is exactly what a synthesised row would do, and a build that faked a plausible decision would pass every other check in the file and fail that one. 8e asserts the lapse carries no operation, decision or refusal; 8f asserts the rendered sentence names no operation either. UNIT TESTS ONLY: case 1 (DASH was closed) and case 3 (the answer DASH could not confirm was delivered). Case 3's runner half runs over the real local transport in tests/runner-server.test.ts and its DASH half - marking the right audit row - is in tests/broker-lapses.test.ts; what is not proven on the installed shell is the two halves meeting, because that needs a child to exit inside the window between DASH deciding and the runner writing. Case 1 cannot be driven by a proof running inside DASH, because it requires DASH not to be running; lib/broker/uptime.ts is tested exhaustively and the wiring in electron/main.ts is not covered by an installed proof. The issue's own account of case 3 was wrong and is corrected in ADR 0005: an undeliverable answer does not leave no trace, because lib/broker/execute.ts audits on every path before the answer travels, so the row already exists and overstates - it became a delivered column on the audit row rather than a second population of near-misses. The new broker_lapses table has no decision, refusal, operation, connection_id or request_id column and tests/store-sqlite.test.ts pins that list. Evidence: pnpm verify green on Windows at this tree - [state] valid, typecheck clean, 60 test files with 1056 passed and 8 skipped, and 63 installed-shell proof checks passed with zero failures plus one advisory note (6l, the live sources, which can never fail a release). Proof 8 passed all six checks on that same first run. Proof 7's ids are now unique per smoke process, which is MAR-473's own lesson pointed the other way: a blocking gate that goes red for a reason unrelated to the change in hand teaches people to re-run it until it is green. THE FINDING IS REAL AND IT IS IN THE PRODUCT: lib/oauth/flow.ts sends no client_secret, in exchangeAuthorizationCode OR refreshAccessToken, and Google answers 'HTTP 400 {error: invalid_request, error_description: client_secret is missing.}' - asked directly, with exactly the parameters DASH sends. DASH's Google OAuth has never worked against real Google and could not have. Filed as MAR-508 (Urgent). This FALSIFIES ADR 0002 amendment 3's point 2 in writing - that a green run would establish the OAuth flow works against Google - and the amendment's guess that G8b, the real MIME projection, was 'the single most likely thing here to have been wrong' was wrong in an instructive direction: the run never reached G8b. Proof 7 passes because the loopback provider's /token is a fixture that cannot refuse for the one reason the real server does, which is exactly the substitution ADR 0002 amendment 1 described and this issue was filed to close. It worked. TWO MORE DEFECTS, both in this harness, neither in product code, filed as MAR-509 and fixed on 000henrik/prove-google-launcher-einval (7da5c54, 800e0f6): (1) it never launched Electron at all - spawnSync of node_modules/.bin/electron.cmd returns EINVAL on current Node since CVE-2024-27980's fix, and result.error was never checked, so two attempts printed the banner and returned to the prompt having done nothing, looking exactly like a proof that ran quietly; (2) it spawned a runner that was never built - runner-process.ts resolves ./runner.mjs relative to its own bundle and nothing built one into dist/google-proof/, reported as never_listened, which reads as a hung runner rather than a missing file. Also: G2 discarded detail and recovery, the only account of WHY, so the first failure could not name itself; once printed, the cause appeared in one line and led straight to MAR-508. WHAT THE RUN DID ESTABLISH, and it is narrow: G0b passed twice, so this was genuinely against https://gmail.googleapis.com with no loopback substitution and the failure is real rather than an artifact of pointing somewhere else; G7a passed, so the runner starts and reports a real named pipe under this harness. Everything about the broker, the projection, the write, the negatives, the audit and the revocation is UNTOUCHED - the run never reached a brokered call, and nothing here is evidence for or against any of it. MACHINE STATE: nothing to clean. No credential reached the vault, so the cleanup had nothing to revoke and no orphan grant exists at Google - confirmed absent from the account's third-party app list. No draft was created and no draft id was printed. THE LESSON THIS ISSUE'S OWN NOTE PREDICTED, pointed one level up: it said a runbook is not a run. A harness that builds is not a harness that runs either. Everything about this harness reachable without a consent screen HAD been validated - typecheck, esbuild bundle, node --check on the generated agent - and all three defects live strictly outside that set. PRIOR NOTE, still accurate about what was BUILT: What was built: scripts/google-proof/main.ts (an Electron main entry, checks G0a-G16), scripts/prove-google.mjs (builds and launches it) and docs/real-google-proof-runbook.md. The design decision that mattered was NOT writing it as a standalone script driving lib/broker/ directly, which is the cheap way. It boots the same shell through the same electron/smoke-identity.ts and electron/main.ts, writes to the same user-data directory, uses the same OS vault, adopts the same runner and spawns a real child speaking the same broker protocol - so the only variable between it and proof 7 is which server answers, plus the pre-consent summary window, which is a renderer surface and not on the path any provider request takes. There is therefore no substrate seam between the two proofs, only one check. That check is 7n: proof 7's harness SERVES Gmail's two send endpoints and answers them with success, which is what makes 'DASH never called a send endpoint' a statement about DASH rather than about a provider's willingness to refuse. Google cannot be made willing, so G12b reads broker_audit instead and is weaker in exactly that way - it would not distinguish a request DASH built and Google rejected from one DASH never built. The asymmetry runs both ways and is why neither proof is redundant: G11 refuses both send attempts against a credential Google would genuinely have honoured, which no loopback grant can model because that grant is a fixture the harness wrote itself. Both stay; proof 7 runs on every commit and this one runs when somebody is watching. G0b is the cheapest check and the one the whole record rests on - loopbackProofOrigin() must be null, or every check below would pass against the fake provider and the dated log would be a lie about which server answered; the run stops there if it fails. It cannot become a gate by construction, not by convention: scripts/prove-google.mjs exits before it builds anything if CI is set or no terminal is attached, and no package.json script names it (ADR 0004). pnpm verify does not run it and DOES typecheck it - tsconfig.json now includes scripts/google-proof - because a proof that rots silently between attended runs would be worse than none, and typechecking a file is not executing it. The write half creates a REAL draft in a REAL Drafts folder, said before the step and behind a typed confirmation; DASH has no operation that deletes a draft and this proof must not be the reason one gets built, so the operator deletes it in Gmail and confirms. The run ends by revoking at Google, which is also check G15b: the agent's next request must come back 'revoked' rather than as a generic failure, a MAR-446 acceptance criterion that until now had only ever been asked of a test server returning a hand-written invalid_grant. Regime when it is run: Testing mode with a named test user. Both scopes are RESTRICTED, a public connection needs Google verification, and restricted-scope data crossing a server needs an annual CASA assessment - none of which a Testing-mode run is evidence about. Testing-mode data-scope grants expire SEVEN DAYS after issue, so the record must carry its date. Evidence for this session, and it is evidence about the HARNESS rather than about Google - the attended proof itself is unexecuted: two full pnpm verify runs on Windows, both green, and the requirement they were run against is that verify still passes WITHOUT this proof in it. Each reported [state] valid with the 6 recorded drift warnings, typecheck clean, 62 test files / 1113 passed / 8 skipped / 0 failed, and 67 installed-shell proof checks with ZERO failures plus the one advisory note (6l, the live sources, which can never fail a release; all three answered, 456-604ms). 67 is unchanged from c6c3406 and that is correct: MAR-421 landed in between and added 9 unit tests and no installed proof, which is why the test count moved from 1104 to 1113 and the proof count did not. What varied between the two runs was the harness and not the product, and the first account of it written here was wrong in a way worth recording. Run 1's exit code did not appear when the run finished, because the smoke leaves the runner running on purpose and that detached process inherits the Tee-Object pipeline's stdout handle, which PowerShell waits on - so the pipeline stayed open with the log complete and locked. That was recorded as an exit code that was never observable, and it was DELAYED rather than lost: run 1 reported VERIFY_EXIT=0 about twenty minutes later, when the runner exited and released the handle. Both runs are therefore exit 0. Run 2 had already been launched through cmd.exe with file redirection, which waits on the child rather than on its grandchildren and recorded exit 0 immediately, and it ADOPTED run 1's runner (pid 40672) rather than starting a new one, which is the designed path. The runner was never stopped to force the issue: it may sit in that process tree and AGENTS.md forbids force-killing it. Separately, and this is as far as an unattended session can validate a proof that requires a consent screen: scripts/google-proof/main.ts is confirmed present in the typecheck program via tsc --listFilesOnly, esbuild bundles the entry cleanly, and the generated agent script was extracted from its template and passed node --check - the escaping bug proof 7 records as costing it several three-minute cycles, ruled out before the first attended run rather than during it. One real defect was found by reading the harness back rather than by running it, and fixed in f64a283: a run that died after G2 would have deleted DASH's copy of a live restricted-scope grant while leaving the grant itself alive at Google for the rest of its seven days, owned by a throwaway proof agent and invisible from DASH - the exact orphan lib/connection-actions.ts refuses to create when a disconnect half-fails, reintroduced by a proof. Revocation now happens on every path and before the vault delete, and the draft id is printed on every path too.
